questions.q: In any Exam $12\%$ student absent, there are two subject Math and English, students who passed in both exam is triple to number of students who failed in both and number of student who passed in math only is $45.45\%$ of student who passed in both. If $29\%$ students of total student in English only then find out the % of students who passed in math ?
questions.s:
[Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Venn Diagram)]

Pen-Free Observation: Present bacche = $88\%$. $45.45\%$ fraction $\frac{5}{11}$ hota hai. Seedha equations likh aur 'Both pass' ko ek variable maan.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Let total students $= 100x$. Present $= 88x$.
Let 'Fail Both' $= y$. Toh 'Pass Both' $= 3y$.
'Only Math' $= \frac{5}{11} \times 3y = \frac{15y}{11}$.
'Only English' $= 29\%$ of total $= 29x$.
Venn Equation: (Only M) + (Only E) + (Pass Both) + (Fail Both) = Present
$\frac{15y}{11} + 29x + 3y + y = 88x$
$\frac{15y}{11} + 4y = 59x \Rightarrow \frac{59y}{11} = 59x \Rightarrow y = 11x$.
Pucha hai Total Passed in Math = (Only Math) + (Pass Both)
$= \frac{15y}{11} + 3y = \frac{15(11x)}{11} + 3(11x) = 15x + 33x = 48x = 48\%$.

Takeaway: Calculation lamba dikhta hai par variables easily cancel ho jate hain. $45.45\% = 5 \times 9.09\% = \frac{5}{11}$ ko pehchanna zaroori tha.

questions.q: A reduction of $7.5\%$ in the cost price of a commodity enables a shopkeeper to purchase 15 kg more than what he previously purchased for a sum of $\text{Rs. } 7,400$. In order to make a profit of $32.5\%$ on the pre-reduction cost price of the commodity, at what price (in Rs) per kg should the commodity be sold?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 1. CPR (Constant Product Ratio)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, ye SSC ka all-time favorite format hai. Jab kharcha fixed (Rs 7400) rakha ho, toh price me aayi girawat ka sidha faida hume bachay gye paison me hota hai. Wahin se naya price nikalta hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Buyer ne paise bacha liye hote agar wo utna hi quantity leta. Us shift se current rate nikal lo aur original pe pahoncho.

Mathematically :-
$$ Saved = 7400 \\times 7.5\\% = 555 \\\\ P_{new} = \\frac{555}{15} = 37 \\\\ P_{old} \\times 92.5\\% = 37 \\implies P_{old} = 40 \\\\ SP_{req} = 40 \\times (1 + 32.5\\%) = 40 \\times \\frac{53}{40} = 53 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Basic variables banao. Ratio solve karo lamba root method aayega.

Mathematically :-
$$ \\frac{7400}{P_{new}} - \\frac{7400}{P_{old}} = 15 \\\\ P_{new} = P_{old} \\times 0.925 \\\\ \\frac{7400}{0.925 P_{old}} - \\frac{7400}{P_{old}} = 15 \\\\ P_{old} = 40 \\implies SP = 53 $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab bhi Quantity increase pucha ho, seedha "Total Amount ka $\%$ girawat / Extra Quantity" = "Current Reduced Price" nikal kar base shift karo.

$\text{Acid} = 20 \times 0.8 = 16L$
$\text{Water} = 4L$
$\frac{16}{20+W} = \frac{50}{100} = \frac{1}{2}$
$32 = 20 + W \implies W = 12L$

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Apples me seedha chain multiply maar aur oranges me percentage remaining compare karke beech ki value nikal. Free ke marks hain!

questions.q: A number is first increased by $12\%$ and then again increased by $23\%$. The number so obtained is now decreased by $34\%$. What is the net increase or decrease percent in the original number (rounded off to the nearest integer)?
questions.s:
The "Pen-Free" Observation First:

Dekh bhai, $12\%$ aur $23\%$ ka pehle net nikal, lagbhag $38\%$ up. Ab isko $34\%$ se girana hai. Result = $1.38 \times 0.66$. $1.38 \times \frac{2}{3}$ karoge toh lagbhag 0.92 aayega. Yani $100$ ki cheez 91 reh gayi. Lagbhag $9\%$ ka decrease.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Net}_1 = 12 + 23 + \frac{12 \times 23}{100} = 37.76\% \\ \text{Final Multiplier} = 1.3776 \times (1 - 0.34) \\ = 1.3776 \times 0.66 \approx 0.9092 \\ \text{Net Change} = 1 - 0.9092 = 0.0908 \implies 9.08\% \text{ decrease} $$

questions.q: In the previous government, party Q was in the opposition. Now increasing the seats by 33.33%, Q is the ruling party and thus party Q enjoys twice the majority than that of party P in the previous government. If there were only two parties P and Q and the fix no. of seats be 500 in the parliament of Hum-Tum, then the no. of seats of the Q in the new government is:
questions.s: Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Deviation: $A + B = K$ and $A' + B' = K$. (Whenever total sum is constant, the actual change in a component equals half the difference of their new and old majorities). The "Pen-Free" Observation First: Dekh bhai, agar Q ki seats 33.33\% (yani $1/3$) badh gayi hain, toh nayi seats purani seats ka $1 + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{4}{3}$ hongi. Iska seedha matlab hai nayi seats 4 ka multiple hongi! Options mein 225 aur 275 sidha eliminate ho gaye. 300 pe cross-verify kar, 10 seconds mein answer match karega. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Bhai jo concept tune image mein bheja hai, ye $A+B=K$ wala Change = $\frac{\text{Final Majority} - \text{Initial Majority}}{2}$ logic ekdam lethal hai aur bheed se 10x aage rakhega! Let purani sarkar mein P ki majority = $1$ unit. Toh Q (opposition) ki majority kya hui? $-1$ unit. Nayi sarkar mein Q ki majority = $2$ units (P ki purani majority ka double). Ab nikal Q ki seats mein kitna exact increment hua is rule se: Increment in Q = $\frac{\text{New Majority} - \text{Old Majority}}{2} = \frac{2 - (-1)}{2} = 1.5$ units. Lekin question ke according, Q ki seats 33.33\% yani purani Q ka $\frac{1}{3}$ badhi hain. So, Q ka $\frac{1}{3}$ = $1.5$ units. $\Rightarrow$ Purani Q = $1.5 \times 3 = 4.5$ units. Nayi Q = Purani Q + Increment = $4.5 + 1.5 = 6$ units. Nayi P = Nayi Q - Majority = $6 - 2 = 4$ units. Total seats = Nayi Q + Nayi P = $6 + 4 = 10$ units. Ab seedha equate kar de: $\Rightarrow 10 \text{ units} = 500 \text{ total seats}$ $\Rightarrow 1 \text{ unit} = 50 \text{ seats}$. Toh Nayi Q ($6 \text{ units}$) = $6 \times 50 = 300$ seats. Boom! Khatam. Method 2 (Concept Builder - Basic Tutors $x$ Method): Total seats = 500. Let purani Q = $3x$, toh Nayi Q = $4x$ (kyuki 33.33\% increase hai). Purani P = $500 - 3x$. Nayi P = $500 - 4x$. Purani Majority (P minus Q) = $(500 - 3x) - 3x = 500 - 6x$. Nayi Majority (Q minus P) = $4x - (500 - 4x) = 8x - 500$. Given condition: Nayi Majority = $2 \times$ Purani Majority $\Rightarrow 8x - 500 = 2(500 - 6x)$ $\Rightarrow 8x - 500 = 1000 - 12x$ $\Rightarrow 20x = 1500$ $\Rightarrow x = 75$. Therefore, Nayi Q = $4x = 4 \times 75 = 300$. Future Exam Takeaway: Tera image wala doubt ekdam solid gold hai! Jab bhi $A+B=K$ ho, directly $\frac{\text{Diff}_2 - \text{Diff}_1}{2}$ lagao to find the net change. Ye elections aur voting wale saare tough questions ko without 'x' uda dega!

questions.q: The monthly salary of a person was 80,000. He used to spend on Family Expenses (E), Taxes (T), Charity (C) and rest were his savings. E was 60% of the income, T was 20% of E, and C was 25% of T. When his salary got raised by 40%, he maintained the percentage level of E, but T became 25% of E and C became 25% of T. The ratio of the savings of his earlier salary to that of his present salary?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, answer ratio me chahiye, toh ₹80,000 ek faaltu trap hai examiner ka! Seedha base 100 se start kar, calc 10 times easy ho jayegi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Base 100 maan kar direct components nikalo aur deduct karo.

Mathematically :-
$$I_1 = 100 \\\\ E_1 = 60 \\ T_1 = 60 \times 0.2 = 12 \\ C_1 = 12 \times 0.25 = 3 \\\\ S_1 = 100 - (60+12+3) = 25 \\\\ I_2 = 140 \\\\ E_2 = 140 \times 0.6 = 84 \\ T_2 = 84 \times 0.25 = 21 \\ C_2 = 21 \times 0.25 = 5.25 \\\\ S_2 = 140 - (84+21+5.25) = 29.75 \\\\ Ratio = 25 : 29.75 = 2500 : 2975 = 100 : 119$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Actual ₹80,000 le kar numbers nikalna.

questions.q: If the area of a square is decreased by 19%, then the diagonal of the square is decreased by:
questions.s:
Tool Triggered: 2. Successive Change

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, Area 2D hota hai aur Diagonal 1D. Area 100 se 81 ho gaya ($19\%$ decrease). 1D par aane ke liye square root nikal. 10 se 9 ho gaya. Sidha $10\%$ decrease!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Scale dimension reduction.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Area Ratio} = 100 : 81 \\ \text{Diagonal (1D) Ratio} = \sqrt{100} : \sqrt{81} \\ = 10 : 9 \\ \text{Decrease} = \frac{1}{10} \times 100 = 10\% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Using standard formulas.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Area} = \frac{d^2}{2} \implies d \propto \sqrt{\text{Area}} \\ A_1 = 100, \quad A_2 = 81 \\ d_1 = \sqrt{2 \times 100} = 10\sqrt{2} \\ d_2 = \sqrt{2 \times 81} = 9\sqrt{2} \\ \% \text{ Decrease} = \frac{10\sqrt{2} - 9\sqrt{2}}{10\sqrt{2}} \times 100 = \frac{1}{10} \times 100 = 10\% $$

Exam Takeaway: 2D se 1D pe aana ho toh seedha square root maro. No extra variable needed.

Find the initial number of T-shirts in the bag?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 4. Cross-Product Method

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, ek side par percentage change hai aur dusri side par real value (40) ka increase. Percentage change ko ratio unit me shift karke dono ratios balance karne honge.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Initial = 5:4. Shirts $60\%$ badhi matlab 5 se 8 ho gayi. Naya ratio 2:3 diya hai. Par yahan shirts 8 hain aur naye me 2 dikha raha hai. Ratio ko 4 se multiply karke same kar de $\implies 8:12$. Ab dekh, T-shirts 4 se 12 hui yani 8 unit badhi. Question ke hisaab se 40 badhi. $8=40 \implies 1=5$. Initial T-shirts $4 \times 5 = 20$. Khatam!

Mathematically :-
$\text{Init} = 5:4$
$S_{new} = 5 \times 1.6 = 8$
$\text{New Ratio} = 2:3 = 8:12$
$\text{Diff } T = 12 - 4 = 8 \text{ units}$
$8 \text{ units} = 40 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = 5$
$T_{init} = 4 \times 5 = 20$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): $5x$ aur $4x$ maan. $5x$ ka $160\% = 8x$. Fir $(8x)/(4x + 40) = 2/3$. Cross multiply karke x nikal.

Mathematically :-
$\frac{5x \times 1.6}{4x + 40} = \frac{2}{3}$
$\frac{8x}{4x + 40} = \frac{2}{3}$
$24x = 8x + 80 \implies 16x = 80 \implies x = 5$
$T_{init} = 4(5) = 20$

Exam Takeaway: Ratio ko kisi ek common parameter pe balance karna seekh lo, saare x wale methods redundant ho jayenge.

questions_hin.q_hi: A fruit seller had some apples and oranges. He sold $25\%$ apples to person A, $30\%$ of the remaining to person B and had 42 apples left. Similarly, he sold $30\%$ oranges to A, 60 oranges to B and had $20\%$ Oranges left. What is the total number of apples and oranges that the fruit seller had initially?

Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change & 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Apples me 'remaining' shabd hai matlab successive multiplication chalega. Oranges me flat value ($60$) hai matlab normal line method (unitary scaling) lagega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Apples me seedha chain multiply maar aur oranges me percentage remaining compare karke beech ki value nikal. Free ke marks hain!

Mathematically :-
$$ A \\times \\frac{3}{4} \\times \\frac{7}{10} = 42 \\\\ A = 80 \\\\ O_{B\\%} = 100\\% - (30\\% + 20\\%) = 50\\% \\\\ 50\\% \\ of \\ O = 60 \\\\ O = 120 \\\\ Total = 80 + 120 = 200 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Apples ko $100x$ maan aur oranges ko $100y$. Fractions isilye best hote hain.

Mathematically :-
$$ Let \\ A = 100x \\\\ A_{left} = 100x - 25x - (0.3 \\times 75x) = 52.5x \\\\ 52.5x = 42 \\implies x = 0.8 \\implies A = 80 \\\\ Let \\ O = 100y \\\\ O_{B} = 100y - 30y - 20y = 50y \\\\ 50y = 60 \\implies y = 1.2 \\implies O = 120 \\\\ Total = 80 + 120 = 200 $$

Exam Takeaway: Question ki language padhte hi samajh aana chahiye ki chain rule (successive) lagana hai ya absolute line scaling lagani hai.

questions_hin.q_hi: A number is first increased by $12\%$ and then again increased by $23\%$. The number so obtained is now decreased by $34\%$. What is the net increase or decrease percent in the original number (rounded off to the nearest integer)?
questions_hin.s_hi:
The "Pen-Free" Observation First:

Dekh bhai, $12\%$ aur $23\%$ ka pehle net nikal, lagbhag $38\%$ up. Ab isko $34\%$ se girana hai. Result = $1.38 \times 0.66$. $1.38 \times \frac{2}{3}$ karoge toh lagbhag 0.92 aayega. Yani $100$ ki cheez 91 reh gayi. Lagbhag $9\%$ ka decrease.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Net}_1 = 12 + 23 + \frac{12 \times 23}{100} = 37.76\% \\ \text{Final Multiplier} = 1.3776 \times (1 - 0.34) \\ = 1.3776 \times 0.66 \approx 0.9092 \\ \text{Net Change} = 1 - 0.9092 = 0.0908 \implies 9.08\% \text{ decrease} $$

Exam Takeaway: Approximation is the real king in TCS pattern! Exact decimals calculate karne baithoge toh agla question chhut jayega.

questions_hin.q_hi: In the previous government, party Q was in the opposition. Now increasing the seats by 33.33%, Q is the ruling party and thus party Q enjoys twice the majority than that of party P in the previous government. If there were only two parties P and Q and the fix no. of seats be 500 in the parliament of Hum-Tum, then the no. of seats of the Q in the new government is:
questions_hin.s_hi: Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Deviation: $A + B = K$ and $A' + B' = K$. (Whenever total sum is constant, the actual change in a component equals half the difference of their new and old majorities). The "Pen-Free" Observation First: Dekh bhai, agar Q ki seats 33.33\% (yani $1/3$) badh gayi hain, toh nayi seats purani seats ka $1 + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{4}{3}$ hongi. Iska seedha matlab hai nayi seats 4 ka multiple hongi! Options mein 225 aur 275 sidha eliminate ho gaye. 300 pe cross-verify kar, 10 seconds mein answer match karega. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Bhai jo concept tune image mein bheja hai, ye $A+B=K$ wala Change = $\frac{\text{Final Majority} - \text{Initial Majority}}{2}$ logic ekdam lethal hai aur bheed se 10x aage rakhega! Let purani sarkar mein P ki majority = $1$ unit. Toh Q (opposition) ki majority kya hui? $-1$ unit. Nayi sarkar mein Q ki majority = $2$ units (P ki purani majority ka double). Ab nikal Q ki seats mein kitna exact increment hua is rule se: Increment in Q = $\frac{\text{New Majority} - \text{Old Majority}}{2} = \frac{2 - (-1)}{2} = 1.5$ units. Lekin question ke according, Q ki seats 33.33\% yani purani Q ka $\frac{1}{3}$ badhi hain. So, Q ka $\frac{1}{3}$ = $1.5$ units. $\Rightarrow$ Purani Q = $1.5 \times 3 = 4.5$ units. Nayi Q = Purani Q + Increment = $4.5 + 1.5 = 6$ units. Nayi P = Nayi Q - Majority = $6 - 2 = 4$ units. Total seats = Nayi Q + Nayi P = $6 + 4 = 10$ units. Ab seedha equate kar de: $\Rightarrow 10 \text{ units} = 500 \text{ total seats}$ $\Rightarrow 1 \text{ unit} = 50 \text{ seats}$. Toh Nayi Q ($6 \text{ units}$) = $6 \times 50 = 300$ seats. Boom! Khatam. Method 2 (Concept Builder - Basic Tutors $x$ Method): Total seats = 500. Let purani Q = $3x$, toh Nayi Q = $4x$ (kyuki 33.33\% increase hai). Purani P = $500 - 3x$. Nayi P = $500 - 4x$. Purani Majority (P minus Q) = $(500 - 3x) - 3x = 500 - 6x$. Nayi Majority (Q minus P) = $4x - (500 - 4x) = 8x - 500$. Given condition: Nayi Majority = $2 \times$ Purani Majority $\Rightarrow 8x - 500 = 2(500 - 6x)$ $\Rightarrow 8x - 500 = 1000 - 12x$ $\Rightarrow 20x = 1500$ $\Rightarrow x = 75$. Therefore, Nayi Q = $4x = 4 \times 75 = 300$. Future Exam Takeaway: Tera image wala doubt ekdam solid gold hai! Jab bhi $A+B=K$ ho, directly $\frac{\text{Diff}_2 - \text{Diff}_1}{2}$ lagao to find the net change. Ye elections aur voting wale saare tough questions ko without 'x' uda dega!

questions_hin.q_hi: The monthly salary of a person was 80,000. He used to spend on Family Expenses (E), Taxes (T), Charity (C) and rest were his savings. E was 60% of the income, T was 20% of E, and C was 25% of T. When his salary got raised by 40%, he maintained the percentage level of E, but T became 25% of E and C became 25% of T. The ratio of the savings of his earlier salary to that of his present salary?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, answer ratio me chahiye, toh ₹80,000 ek faaltu trap hai examiner ka! Seedha base 100 se start kar, calc 10 times easy ho jayegi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Base 100 maan kar direct components nikalo aur deduct karo.

Mathematically :-
$$I_1 = 100 \\\\ E_1 = 60 \\ T_1 = 60 \times 0.2 = 12 \\ C_1 = 12 \times 0.25 = 3 \\\\ S_1 = 100 - (60+12+3) = 25 \\\\ I_2 = 140 \\\\ E_2 = 140 \times 0.6 = 84 \\ T_2 = 84 \times 0.25 = 21 \\ C_2 = 21 \times 0.25 = 5.25 \\\\ S_2 = 140 - (84+21+5.25) = 29.75 \\\\ Ratio = 25 : 29.75 = 2500 : 2975 = 100 : 119$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Actual ₹80,000 le kar numbers nikalna.

Mathematically :-
$$I_1 = 80000 \\\\ E_1 = 48000, \ T_1 = 9600, \ C_1 = 2400 \Rightarrow S_1 = 20000 \\\\ I_2 = 112000 \\\\ E_2 = 67200, \ T_2 = 16800, \ C_2 = 4200 \Rightarrow S_2 = 23800 \\\\ Ratio = 20000 : 23800 = 200 : 238 = 100 : 119$$

Exam Takeaway: Jab ratios hi pucha ho toh actual numbers ko use karna ek time-killing trap hota hai. Ignore them completely.

[Core Tool Triggered: JSM / Deviation (Tree Diagram)]

Pen-Free Observation: Data straight hai, base $100$ maan kar split kar de. Total men 40, women 60 hain. Target 'women $\le 38k$' nikalna hai.



Method 1 isme tum female ka % nikalne ke bajay tum female ka total pop se compare karne lagte ho jo ki galat hai aisa repeated karte ho(Ninja Technique):

Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

$$ H_1 = \\frac{5}{8} \\\\ H_{rem} = 1 - \\frac{5}{8} = \\frac{3}{8} \\\\ H_2 = \\frac{3}{8} \\times \\frac{1}{8} = \\frac{3}{64} \\\\ Distance = 192 \\times \\frac{3}{64} = 9 \\ m $$

Mathematically :-
$$ D_1 = 192 \\times 0.625 = 120 \\ m \\\\ Rem = 192 - 120 = 72 \\ m \\\\ D_2 = 72 \\times 0.125 = 9 \\ m $$

questions_hin.q_hi: In an election between two candidates, y% of the voters did not vote. 10% of the votes cast were declared invalid, while all the valid votes were cast in favour of either of the two candidates. **Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):** Winner ko 59.375\% mile toh Loser ko $100 - 59.375 = 40.625\%$. Margin aya $18.75\%$. Iska fraction banao $\frac{3}{16}$. **Method 2 (Concept Builder):** Chain equation banti: $16000 \times (1 - \frac{y}{100}) \times 0.9 \times 0.1875 = 2484$. Is equation me ekmatra unknown $y$ hai. Equation build karo aur direct fraction value se break karo.

questions_hin.q_hi: If the area of a square is decreased by 19%, then the diagonal of the square is decreased by:
questions_hin.s_hi:
Tool Triggered: 2. Successive Change

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, Area 2D hota hai aur Diagonal 1D. Area 100 se 81 ho gaya ($19\%$ decrease). 1D par aane ke liye square root nikal. 10 se 9 ho gaya. Sidha $10\%$ decrease!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Scale dimension reduction.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Area Ratio} = 100 : 81 \\ \text{Diagonal (1D) Ratio} = \sqrt{100} : \sqrt{81} \\ = 10 : 9 \\ \text{Decrease} = \frac{1}{10} \times 100 = 10\% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Using standard formulas.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Area} = \frac{d^2}{2} \implies d \propto \sqrt{\text{Area}} \\ A_1 = 100, \quad A_2 = 81 \\ d_1 = \sqrt{2 \times 100} = 10\sqrt{2} \\ d_2 = \sqrt{2 \times 81} = 9\sqrt{2} \\ \% \text{ Decrease} = \frac{10\sqrt{2} - 9\sqrt{2}}{10\sqrt{2}} \times 100 = \frac{1}{10} \times 100 = 10\% $$

Exam Takeaway: 2D se 1D pe aana ho toh seedha square root maro. No extra variable needed.

questions_hin.q_hi: Ratio of the number of shirts and T-shirts in the bag is 5:4. Find the initial number of T-shirts in the bag?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: 4. Cross-Product Method

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, ek side par percentage change hai aur dusri side par real value (40) ka increase. Percentage change ko ratio unit me shift karke dono ratios balance karne honge.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Initial = 5:4. Shirts $60\%$ badhi matlab 5 se 8 ho gayi. Naya ratio 2:3 diya hai. Par yahan shirts 8 hain aur naye me 2 dikha raha hai. Ratio ko 4 se multiply karke same kar de $\implies 8:12$. Ab dekh, T-shirts 4 se 12 hui yani 8 unit badhi. Question ke hisaab se 40 badhi. $8=40 \implies 1=5$. Initial T-shirts $4 \times 5 = 20$. Khatam!

Mathematically :-
$\text{Init} = 5:4$
$S_{new} = 5 \times 1.6 = 8$
